theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is the main job of a welding supervisor on a fabrication job?
options: To do all of the hardest welds himself on every single shift
To sign the welders' time sheets and nothing else
To buy the steel and arrange the delivery trucks
To see welding is done safely, to the WPS and drawings

questions.stem: Before welding starts on a job to an AWS code, which check by the welding supervisor comes first?
options: That the welders have brought their own helmets
That each WPS covers its joints and is approved
That the paint for the finished job has arrived
That the client has paid the first invoice

questions.stem: A welder's record shows a 3G plate test on 10 mm carbon steel with E7018. The job is a 6G pipe joint. What should the supervisor decide?
options: He is not covered: use a pipe-qualified welder or test him
He is covered, as a vertical plate test covers all pipe work
He is covered if he uses the same electrode as his test
He is covered if another welder checks his root pass

questions.stem: Why does a supervisor keep a log of when each qualified welder last used each welding process?
options: So overtime can be shared out fairly each month
So the store knows which electrodes to reorder
A qualification can lapse if a process is not used for a set time
So the welders can each be paid a bonus for every process they use

questions.stem: Why is each welder on a coded job given an identity number or stamp to mark beside his welds?
options: So the welders can claim their work for a bonus
So the client can choose which welder to hire next
So the paint shop knows which welds to paint first
So each weld can be traced to the welder who made it

questions.stem: Radiography shows welder A has 2 repairs in 50 joints and welder B has 9 repairs in 45 joints. What should the supervisor do first?
options: Look at welder B's welds and method, then coach or retest him
Give welder B all the easy joints and say nothing to him
Stop sending welder A's joints for any more radiography
Ask the radiographer to pass more of welder B's joints from now on

questions.stem: Welder B had 9 repairs in 45 radiographed joints. What is his repair rate?
On a coded job, who should control the issue of low-hydrogen electrodes to the welders?
options: Each welder, taking what he likes from the store
Whoever happens to be nearest the oven at the time
A named person, using the oven log and issue rules
The delivery driver, when the electrodes arrive

questions.stem: A welder is found using E6013 electrodes on a joint whose WPS calls for E7018. What should the supervisor do?
options: Stop him, hold the welds made, and report it
Let him finish the joint, then switch rods
Tell him to use E7018 on the cap only
Say nothing, as both are mild steel rods

questions.stem: A welder is running passes one after another on a small part without checking the joint temperature. The WPS gives a maximum interpass temperature. What should the supervisor do?
options: Let him carry on, as small parts always cool down very fast
Tell him to cool the part in a bucket of water
Ask him to weld faster so less heat builds up
Have him check and keep within the limit, and record it

questions.stem: A welder is working from a drawing marked revision B. The office issued revision C yesterday. What should the supervisor do?
options: Let him finish to revision B and use C next time
Mark the changes on revision B from memory
Stop, check what changed, and swap in revision C
Keep both copies at the booth so he can choose

questions.stem: A drawing calls for a fillet weld that cannot fit the joint as detailed. What should the supervisor do?
options: Tell the welder to make the biggest weld he can fit
Raise a query with the engineer and get a written answer
Change the drawing himself and carry on with the job
Leave the weld out and tell the client about it at the handover

questions.stem: Why does a fire watch stay at the site for a time after hot work has ended?
options: To clean up the slag and stubs for the welder
To check the welds have cooled before painting
To guard the welding set from being taken
Smouldering material can burst into flame later

questions.stem: A welder must weld inside a water tank. Before he goes in, what must the supervisor arrange?
options: A permit, a gas test, ventilation and a standby person
A longer welding lead and a brighter work lamp, and nothing more
A fan blowing pure oxygen into the tank to freshen it
A radio, so the welder can call when he is finished

questions.stem: Why must gas cylinders never be taken into a tank where welding is going on?
options: They take up the room the welder needs to move about inside it
They make the tank too heavy for its stand
A leak can fill the space, causing fire or suffocation
They block the light from the work lamp

questions.stem: A supervisor sees fume hanging in a bay where six welders are working. What is the best first action?
options: Tell the welders to hold their breath when welding
Improve the extraction and check the welders' RPE
Open the bay doors and carry on as before
Move the welders' lunch area further away

questions.stem: A welder works an 8-hour shift and the arc is on for 2.4 hours. What is his operator factor (arc-on time as a share of the shift)?
Which change would most raise the operator factor of a welding crew?
options: Longer tea breaks so welders are well rested
Asking welders to fetch their own steel from the yard
Making each welder grind and fit all of his own parts
Having parts fitted and ready, so welders do not wait

questions.stem: A welder costs J$1 800 an hour. A joint took 3 hours, of which 30 minutes was repair work. What did the repair cost in labour?
Two welders are to weld a long box girder. Which instruction from the supervisor best controls distortion?
options: Each welder starts at one end and works as fast as he possibly can
Follow a set sequence, with the two welders balancing each other
Weld one side fully, then turn the girder and do the other
Use the largest electrodes so the job is over quickly

questions.stem: A weld has failed radiography. Before it is repaired, what should the supervisor make sure of?
options: There is a repair procedure, and the welder is qualified for it
The repair is done by the same welder, whatever his record
The defect is ground out and filled with any electrode
The repair is done quickly, before the client's inspector returns to site

questions.stem: How many times may the same area of a weld usually be repaired?
options: As many times as it takes to pass
Never: a failed weld is always scrapped
Only as many times as the code or client allows
Twice, and then it can be passed anyway

questions.stem: Radiography is to be done in the shop at night. What must the supervisor arrange for his crew?
options: Work on, but stand behind a steel plate
Leave the shop lights off so that the radiography film is not spoiled
Watch the radiographers to learn the method
Keep out of the barriered area, as the radiographers direct

questions.stem: The client's inspector must release a joint at a hold point but cannot come until tomorrow. The crew wants to carry on. What should the supervisor do?
options: Carry on and show the inspector photos tomorrow
Plan other work and wait for the inspector's release
Ask a welder to sign the release in his place
Cover the joint with the next pass to save time

questions.stem: A labour agency sends two welders for a coded job. What should the supervisor check before they start?
options: Their qualification records match the job and are current
That they have brought their own tools and their own transport
That they can start early and work late
That they have worked for the agency before

questions.stem: When a welder qualification test is being done, why must the supervisor or inspector watch the whole test?
options: To time the welder so his speed can be ranked
To help the welder if his root goes wrong
To confirm he made it to the WPS without help
To pick the best part of the plate to test

questions.stem: Why does a supervisor make sure that each welding set's cables, holders and earth clamps are checked and tagged at set intervals?
options: So the sets can be sold for a better price
So the welders know whose set is whose
So the electricity bill can be shared fairly
Damaged leads cause shocks, burns and poor welds

questions.stem: A trainee welder is keen but not yet qualified. How may the supervisor use him on a coded job?
options: On uncoded tasks, such as fit-up help, until he qualifies
On the coded welds, as long as a qualified welder signs for them
On the root passes only, where no one can see them
Nowhere at all on the site until he is qualified

questions.stem: Which belongs in a welding supervisor's daily report?
options: The welders' home addresses and family details
Welds done, by whom, issues, tests and delays
Only the hours worked by each welder that day
A list of the welders' favourite machines

questions.stem: Several welders find the WPS hard to read. What is the best way to make sure they follow it?
options: Leave it at the office, as the welders know the job
Tell them to ask the client if they are unsure
Go through it at the job and post a key-settings sheet
Let each welder use the settings he feels are right

questions.stem: A strong breeze is blowing across a site where GMAW is being used on a steel frame in Montego Bay. What should the supervisor decide?
options: Turn the gas flow up as high as it will go
Carry on, as the breeze helps to keep the welders cool in the sun
Tell the welders to work faster before it rains
Screen the joints, or use a process the WPS allows outdoors

questions.stem: Under workplace safety law, what is a supervisor's duty when he sees one of his crew working unsafely?
options: Report it at the end of the week in writing
Stop it and put it right, as he is responsible for the crew
Ignore it if the job is behind programme
Leave it to the safety officer to notice it on his next site walk

questions.stem: A welder gets an electric shock from his set but says he is fine. What should the supervisor do?
options: Stop the work, get him checked, isolate the set and report
Let him carry on if he feels well enough
Tell him to wear a second pair of gloves
Swap his set with another welder's set and move on with the job

questions.stem: Welders are working inside a steel tank on a hot July afternoon in Clarendon. What should the supervisor do about the heat?
options: Nothing: welders are used to the heat
Tell them to finish quickly and then rest
Plan breaks, water and cooler hours, and watch for signs
Let them take off their jackets and gloves so that they keep cool

questions.stem: Offcuts of plate are being used to make gussets on a coded job. What must the supervisor check?
options: That the offcuts are the cleanest in the yard
That the offcuts are cut with a plasma cutter
That the gussets are painted before welding
That the heat number is copied so it can be traced

questions.stem: A welder qualified on 10 mm plate is to weld 40 mm plate on the job. What should the supervisor check?
options: That the welder has done thick plate before at home
Whether his test thickness covers 40 mm under the code
That the 40 mm plate is preheated by the welder
That the welder uses a larger electrode on the root

questions.stem: A good welder suddenly has many rejected welds. What is the best first step for the supervisor?
options: Talk with him and check his set, consumables and conditions
Send him for a new qualification test at once
Move him to cleaning duties for the rest of the job until it ends
Warn him in front of the crew so others take note

questions.stem: Before a coded job starts, what should the supervisor's briefing to the welders cover?
options: Only the finish date and the overtime rates
The client's company history and its owners
The WPS, sequence, hold points, hazards and roles
Which welders will be laid off when the job ends

questions.stem: Shielding gas use has doubled this week on the same kind of work. What should the supervisor check first?
options: Whether the gas supplier has raised its prices
For leaks in hoses and fittings, and the flow settings
Whether the welders are welding more slowly
Whether the cylinders are standing in the sun

questions.stem: Electrode stubs about 100 mm long are being thrown away. What should the supervisor do?
options: Order longer electrodes from the supplier
Collect the stubs and weld with them later
Nothing, as stubs are always that length
Coach the welders to use each rod to a short stub

questions.stem: To meet a deadline, the client's site manager asks the supervisor to skip a test that the specification calls for. What should he do?
options: Refer it to his manager; tests change only in writing
Skip it, as the client is always right
Do the test later, after the job has been handed over to the client
Skip it, but write it up as done in the records

questions.stem: At handover of a coded job, which welding records should go in the job file?
options: The welders' time sheets and wage slips
Photos of the crew taken at the end-of-job lunch
WPSs, welder records, weld map, tests and repairs
The delivery notes for the paint and the bolts

questions.stem: A grinder is being used beside a welder in the next bay, with no screens between them. What should the supervisor do?
options: Tell the welder to move his booth further away when he has time
Put up screens and direct the sparks away from people
Let them carry on, as grinding sparks are harmless
Ask the grinder operator to grind only after dark

questions.stem: Who signs to confirm that a welder has passed his qualification test?
options: The welder himself, after he sees the results
The store keeper who gave out the electrodes
Any welder who worked beside him on the day
The examiner or inspector who watched and judged it

essays.stem: Describe the main duties of a welding supervisor before, during and after a welding job to an AWS code.
essays.modelAnswer: Before the job, the supervisor reads the drawings and specification, checks that an approved WPS covers every joint, and checks each welder's qualification and continuity. He makes sure the materials and consumables are correct and traceable, the equipment is safe and tested, and the permits and safety controls are in place. He plans the sequence and the crew, and briefs the welders on the WPS, hold points and hazards. During the job, he checks fit-up, preheat, settings, interpass, cleaning and consumable control, watches for unsafe acts, deals with problems and queries, arranges inspections at hold points, and keeps daily records. After the job, he makes sure all welds are inspected and tested, repairs are closed out and re-tested, the area is left safe, and the records (WPSs, welder records, weld map, tests and repairs) are complete for handover. Throughout, he coaches the crew and reports to management.
markingPoints: Before: drawings, WPS approval, welder qualifications, materials, equipment, permits
Before: plans the work and briefs the crew
During: in-process checks of fit-up, preheat, settings, consumables and safety
During: hold points, problems, daily records
After: inspection and repairs closed, area safe, records complete for handover

essays.stem: Explain how you would make sure that every welder on a coded job is qualified for the joints given to them, and that their qualifications stay current through the job.
essays.modelAnswer: I would make a qualification matrix listing each welder against the processes, positions, materials, thickness and diameter ranges their tests cover, using their signed qualification records. I would compare it with the weld map, so that each joint goes only to a welder whose range covers it. For any gap, I would use another welder or arrange a test, witnessed and judged by an inspector, before that welder works on the joint. Agency or new welders show their records before they start, and I check they are genuine and current. To keep qualifications current, I keep a continuity log showing when each welder last used each process, and I check it each month, because a qualification can lapse if a process is not used for a set time under the code. I also watch repair rates by welder; if a welder's work falls off, I may ask for a retest. The matrix and log go in the job file.
markingPoints: Qualification matrix from signed records: process, position, material, thickness ranges
Joints allocated only within each welder's range, checked against the weld map
Gaps filled with another welder or a witnessed test
New and agency welders' records checked before starting
Continuity log and repair rates used to keep qualifications current; records filed

essays.stem: Explain how you would control welding consumables on a coded job, from the time they arrive until unused ones are returned.
essays.modelAnswer: When electrodes, wire, flux and gas arrive, I check them against the WPS and the order: class, size, batch or lot number and certificates, and that packets are sealed and undamaged. Damaged or doubtful stock is quarantined. Consumables are stored in a dry, locked store, by type, with first in, first out. Low-hydrogen electrodes and flux are baked or kept in ovens at the maker's temperature, and the oven temperatures are logged each shift. A named person issues consumables against the WPS for each joint, in small amounts, and records who received which batch and when on an issue log. Welders keep low-hydrogen electrodes in heated quivers. At the end of the shift, unused electrodes are returned and re-dried or scrapped as the maker says, and stubs are counted. Gas cylinders are checked for the right gas, chained up and logged. These records let any fault be traced to the batch.
markingPoints: Receipt checks against WPS and order, with certificates; quarantine of doubtful stock
Dry, secure storage and stock rotation
Ovens and quivers for low-hydrogen consumables, with temperature logs
Controlled issue by a named person, with an issue log
Returns re-dried or scrapped as the maker says; traceability

essays.stem: A welder's repair rate on radiographed joints has risen from 3% to 15% over two weeks. Explain how you would deal with it as the welding supervisor.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would look at the facts: which joints failed, what defects were found, in which positions, and whether anything changed, such as a new batch of electrodes, a new machine or a new kind of joint. Then I would talk with the welder in private, without blame, to hear his view, and check his set, leads, consumables, fit-up and working conditions, such as wind, poor lighting or tiredness. I would watch him weld to see his technique and his settings against the WPS. If the cause is equipment or materials, I would fix it. If it is technique, I would coach him on that defect and let him practise on test pieces. If the problem goes on, I would take him off coded work and arrange a retest. I would have all his recent joints checked, record the actions, and follow his repair rate in the next weeks to see that it falls back.
markingPoints: Collects facts: defects, positions, changes
Private, fair talk with the welder
Checks equipment, consumables, fit-up, conditions and technique against the WPS
Fixes the cause: coaching, practice, or retest and removal from coded work
Recent work checked, actions recorded and repair rate followed up

essays.stem: Describe how you would plan and supervise welding inside a confined space, such as a steel water tank.
essays.modelAnswer: I would first ask whether the work can be done from outside. If not, I would get a confined space entry permit and a hot work permit. The tank is isolated from all pipes and power, cleaned and ventilated. Before entry, a trained person tests the air with a gas detector for oxygen, flammable gas and toxic gas, and tests again during the work. Forced ventilation and fume extraction are set up. Gas cylinders and welding sets stay outside, and hoses and leads are checked and removed when not in use. Only trained people go in, with a standby person outside who stays in contact and can raise the alarm, and a rescue plan and equipment are ready. Lighting is low-voltage. Welders take breaks for heat and wear suitable PPE. Fire watch continues after the work. I would brief the crew, check the controls myself, and close the permits when the space is clear.
markingPoints: Avoid entry if possible; confined space and hot work permits
Isolation, cleaning, gas testing before and during work, ventilation
Cylinders and sets outside; leads and hoses checked
Trained entrants, standby person and a rescue plan
Heat breaks, PPE, fire watch, briefing and closing the permits

essays.stem: Explain how a welding supervisor can raise the output of a welding crew without lowering quality or safety.
essays.modelAnswer: Output depends on how much of the shift the arc is burning (the operator factor) and how fast weld metal is laid. I would measure the arc time and look at where time is lost: waiting for parts, fetching materials, poor fit-up, repairs and moving equipment. I would have fitters prepare and tack parts ahead of the welders, keep consumables and gas at the work station, and use positioners and turning rolls so that more welds are flat or horizontal, which are faster and give fewer defects. Where the WPS allows, a higher-deposition process such as FCAW or SAW can be used on long welds. Avoiding over-welding beyond the drawing size saves time and reduces distortion. Cutting the repair rate through coaching saves the most, because repairs cost several times the original weld. Breaks and safe working hours stay in place, because tired welders make mistakes. I would track output and repairs each week.
markingPoints: Explains operator factor and deposition rate
Finds and cuts lost time: fit-up ahead, materials at hand
Positioners and flat or horizontal welding
Higher-deposition process where the WPS allows; no over-welding
Reducing repairs, keeping safe hours, and tracking results

essays.stem: Describe how a weld repair should be managed under the welding supervisor, from the moment a defect is found until the repair is closed.
essays.modelAnswer: When a defect is found, the weld is marked, and the defect's type, size and position are recorded on an inspection report or non-conformance report. The supervisor checks whether a repair is allowed and how many times, under the code or contract, and gets the repair procedure approved. A qualified welder is chosen; often a different welder if the first keeps failing. The defect is removed by grinding or gouging, and the excavation is checked by dye penetrant or magnetic particle testing to be sure it is all gone. The groove is shaped so it can be welded well, preheat is applied if the procedure says, and the repair is welded to the repair procedure. The repair is then inspected and tested again by the same method that found the defect. The results, the welder and the consumables are recorded on the weld map, and the report is closed. The supervisor also looks for the cause to stop it happening again.
markingPoints: Defect marked and recorded on a report
Repair allowed and procedure approved; qualified welder chosen
Defect removed and the excavation checked before welding
Repair welded to procedure, with preheat if needed
Re-tested by the same method, recorded, report closed, cause addressed

essays.stem: Explain the extra points a welding supervisor must manage when welding a steel frame on an outdoor site, such as a hotel extension on the north coast.
essays.modelAnswer: Weather is the first point. Wind blows away shielding gas, so joints are screened or a process the WPS allows outdoors is used. Rain and wet steel cause porosity and shock risk, so work stops or the joint is sheltered and dried. Strong sun heats steel and people, so breaks and water are planned. Hot work needs a permit, cleared combustibles, extinguishers and a fire watch, especially near timber or guests. The public and other trades must be kept away from arc flash and falling sparks with screens and barriers. Work at height needs safe access and fall protection, and gas cylinders and sets must be secured. Power from a generator or site supply must be safe, with earthing and protected cables. Consumables must be kept dry in a site store or ovens. The supervisor also arranges site inspection, coordinates with the site manager and records the daily conditions.
markingPoints: Wind and rain: screening, sheltering, stopping, porosity and shock risks
Heat and breaks
Hot work permit, fire watch and protection of the public
Work at height, secure cylinders and safe power supply
Dry storage of consumables, coordination and daily records

essays.stem: Explain the welding supervisor's role in working with the client's inspector and the testing company on a coded job.
essays.modelAnswer: The supervisor agrees the inspection and test plan with the client's inspector before work starts, so both know the hold points, witness points and tests. He gives the inspector notice when a stage is ready and does not cover work at a hold point until it is released. He makes the records available: WPSs, welder qualifications, consumable logs and preheat records. He books the testing company in good time and has the welds clean, numbered and accessible. For radiography, he clears his crew from the barriered area and follows the radiographers' instructions, often planning it at night or at breaks. When results come in, he checks them against the weld map, arranges repairs to procedure and re-tests, and tracks results by welder. He stays polite and open, records agreements in writing, and refers anything that changes the specification to his manager.
markingPoints: Agrees the inspection and test plan, hold and witness points
Gives notice and never covers work at a hold point
Provides records and prepares welds for testing
Radiography safety and scheduling
Acts on results, records agreements and refers specification changes

essays.stem: Describe the records a welding supervisor keeps on a coded job, and explain how they are used at handover and afterwards.
essays.modelAnswer: The supervisor keeps the approved WPSs and their PQRs, the welder qualification records and continuity log, and a qualification matrix. He keeps the material certificates with heat numbers, and the consumable receipt, oven and issue logs. A weld map numbers every weld, and each weld's welder, date, consumable batch, preheat and inspection results are recorded. Inspection and NDT reports, repair records and non-conformance reports are kept, along with daily reports, permits and toolbox talk records. At handover, these go into the job file or data book for the client, showing that every weld was made by a qualified welder to an approved procedure and passed its tests. Afterwards, if a fault appears in service, the records let the firm trace the weld to its welder, materials and tests, and find the cause. They also help to price and plan the next job, and to defend the firm if there is a dispute.
markingPoints: Procedure and welder records: WPS, PQR, qualifications, continuity
Material and consumable records
Weld map with per-weld details; inspection, NDT, repair and NCR records
Daily reports, permits and briefings
Use at handover (data book) and afterwards (traceability, planning, disputes)

practical1.title: Supervise a small coded welding job: qualification matrix, briefing, consumable issue and daily report
practical1.brief: The assessor gives the group a small welding job to a WPS (for example, fillet welding six brackets to a base plate), the qualification records of each member (made up for the task), and a weld map. Each member takes a turn as the supervisor for one stage of the job while the others weld, fit or inspect. Stage 1: build a qualification matrix and allocate each weld on the weld map to a member whose record covers it. Stage 2: give a five-minute pre-job briefing on the WPS, sequence, hold points and hazards. Stage 3: run consumable control: issue electrodes or wire against the WPS and fill in the issue log. Stage 4: supervise the welding: check fit-up, settings and safety, and stop and correct any problem. Stage 5: inspect the finished welds with the group, mark them on the weld map and write the daily report. If the group has five members, the fifth supervises the clean-up and the return of consumables. Every member welds at least one joint. Photograph each stage.
materials: Job drawing, WPS and weld map (from the assessor)
Made-up qualification records for each member
Steel brackets and base plates for the job
Welding sets, electrodes or wire, and an electrode oven if used
Qualification matrix, issue log, weld log and daily report forms
Fillet weld gauges, steel rule and marker
photos: The completed qualification matrix and the allocated weld map
The issue log being filled in as consumables are given out
The supervisor checking a fit-up or a setting during welding
The finished welds marked on the weld map
checklist: Allocated welds only to members whose records cover them
Gave a clear briefing covering the WPS, sequence, hold points and hazards
Issued consumables against the WPS and recorded the issue correctly
Checked fit-up and settings and stopped or corrected a problem when one arose
Welded at least one joint to the WPS
Inspected and recorded the welds accurately on the weld map
Wrote a clear daily report with welds done, issues and actions
safety: The supervisor of each stage is responsible for stopping unsafe work
Weld in booths or behind screens, with fume extraction
Wear full PPE when welding or watching the welding
Keep the area clear of anything that burns, with an extinguisher at hand

practical2.title: Supervision role play: handle five staged welding problems and record the actions
practical2.brief: The assessor sets up five problems around the welding bays, each with a card and the props needed. For example: a welder about to start a pipe joint his record does not cover; E6013 electrodes at a booth where the WPS calls for E7018; a joint being welded without the preheat the WPS gives; hot work beside cardboard with no fire watch; and a welding lead with damaged insulation. As a group, first agree how a supervisor should deal with each kind of problem. Then each member leads one problem as the supervisor, while the others play the welder, the inspector or the manager: the supervisor stops the work if needed, explains the problem in plain words, puts it right, and records it on an action record or a non-conformance report. In a group of four, the assessor plays the fifth problem. Finally, the group writes a one-page summary of the five problems, their causes and how each could be prevented, and presents it to the assessor. Photograph each problem before and after it is dealt with.
materials: Five problem cards and props set up by the assessor
